hypothesis: Under 9a4caa7b defaults (bf16_norm_output=False, bf16_sdpa_input=False) the LM-head logits projection executes with FP32 operands. With only 55.7M dense parameters (no-ngram-ve ledger row) the vocab projection is a large share of dense matmul FLOPs and materializes the largest activation in the network (B x T x V logits), so it is a measurable per-step cost. Executing that single matmul with BF16 operands (FP32 master weight, FP32 logits restored immediately for softcap/CE/eval) will raise the fixed-budget step count by >=2% (the analogous isolated BF16-SDPA boundary gave 2233 vs 2076 steps, 1.002028 vs 1.005967 BPB) while BF16 rounding of the head matmul costs less quality than the recovered steps buy, lowering public_val_bpb by >=0.001 versus the same-host pinned control.
implementation_plan: All edits confined to train.py on branch autoloop/20260922-bf16-lm-head-helper-cpu-verified-r4 from 9a4caa7b. STEP 0 (static check, written to the experiment directory as step0_head_dtypes.md BEFORE any edit, with quoted line ranges): locate the final logits projection -- the F.linear / matmul / tied wte-weight product mapping the final-normed hidden state [B,T,d] to vocab logits immediately upstream of softcap and cross-entropy (region gated by --nki-softcap-ce and --byte-loss-weight). Record under default flags (bf16_norm_output False, bf16_sdpa_input False): (a) dtype of the activation entering the head call (trace from norm() lines 1446-1462), (b) whether the head goes through the Linear class and, if so, which weight tensor Linear.forward (lines ~3174-3189) actually passes to the matmul for an FP32 input (FP32 master vs cached copy, detached or not), (c) how gradients reach the FP32 master, (d) whether any torch.autocast context encloses the call, (e) whether --transposed-linear selects a transposed mirror at the head. If both operands are already BF16 or the call is under autocast, stop and return HALT-INERT. STEP 1 (helper): add one module-level function near the Linear class: def lm_head_logits(h, weight, enabled): if not enabled: return <the exact original expression currently used at the head, passing h and weight unchanged>; h16 = h.to(torch.bfloat16); w16 = weight.to(torch.bfloat16); return <the same expression form with h16, w16>.float(). 'weight' must be the FP32 master tensor the original code uses (lm_head.weight or tied wte.weight, or the transposed mirror if that layout is active -- keep the existing layout, do not change tying, create Parameters, or alter init). The .to() casts are ordinary differentiable casts, NOT detached cache copies, so autograd accumulates the FP32 master gradient through the cast. If the original head call is Linear.forward, the helper's enabled branch must bypass Linear.forward and call F.linear (or the layout-equivalent matmul recorded in STEP 0) directly on h16/w16 so both operands are provably BF16; the disabled branch must call exactly the original code path. Replace the single head call site with lm_head_logits(h, weight, USE_BF16_LM_HEAD). The same forward code serves training and evaluation; no separate eval branch. STEP 2 (toggle): following the existing --bf16-sdpa-input pattern, add module-level USE_BF16_LM_HEAD = True with env override NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_LM_HEAD ('0' disables), argparse pair --bf16-lm-head / --no-bf16-lm-head (dest bf16_lm_head, default None -> constant), and append 'USE_BF16_LM_HEAD' to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES (lines ~5251-5266) so checkpoints persist it and load_for_eval() restores it; default must resolve True so the candidate run uses no flags. STEP 3 (logging): add exactly one field 'bf16_lm_head=<bool>' to the existing precision-options config oneliner. No runtime dtype logger inside the compiled forward is required or permitted. STEP 4 (offline CPU verification, mandatory, saved as step4_cpu_check.txt): run a small CPU script that imports the helper from train.py (or execs the function source) and, with h = torch.randn(2,4,d, requires_grad=True) and weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(V,d)) both float32 (small d,V such as 8,16 are fine): (i) enabled=True: wrap torch.nn.functional.linear/matmul via a forward hook or monkeypatch to capture operand dtypes and assert both are torch.bfloat16; assert output dtype is torch.float32; call out.sum().backward(); assert weight.grad is not None and weight.grad.dtype == torch.float32 and h.grad.dtype == torch.float32; (ii) enabled=False: assert output equals the original expression exactly (torch.equal) and captured operand dtypes are float32. STEP 5 (artifacts for the implementation verifier, all in the experiment directory): (a) full diff limited to the helper, the single call-site replacement, toggle/env/CLI resolution, the ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES entry, and the one config-log field; (b) grep output showing softcap/CE/byte-loss/eval-accumulation/causality code untouched; (c) step0_head_dtypes.md; (d) step4_cpu_check.txt; (e) quoted checkpoint save code and load_for_eval() code showing USE_BF16_LM_HEAD is persisted and restored; (f) statement that with NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_LM_HEAD=0 the helper's disabled branch executes the original expression (proven by step4 (ii)). Smoke evidence (bf16_lm_head=True in the oneliner, num_params_M 592.9, ngram_ve and other oneliners identical to control, causality_passed True, smoke gate >=342 steps, step-rate ratio >=1.02, public_val_bpb <= control smoke + 0.003) is produced by the Operator's standard smoke run and evaluated by the smoke gate, not required from the Implementer. Launch the full run with the exact control launch command and environment (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4 train.py --num-steps 5000 --max-train-seconds 1800 --seed 42, NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1) and no additional flags.
single_causal_change: One numerical-format boundary change confined to train.py: at the LM-head logits projection only, both matmul operands (final-normed hidden activation and the head weight, tied or untied) are temporary BF16 tensors produced by differentiable .to(torch.bfloat16) casts of the FP32 tensors the current code uses; the matmul executes in BF16; the logits are immediately cast .float() so softcap, cross-entropy, byte-loss weighting, eval BPB accumulation and the causality check consume FP32 logits through untouched downstream code. The boundary is implemented as one isolated module-level helper so its operand/output dtypes and FP32-master gradient routing are verified offline on CPU before any Trn2 launch (this is the fix for the r3 implementation-review defects: missing pre-edit STEP 0 artifact, missing disabled-path demonstration, unquoted checkpoint/load_for_eval parity, and a dtype log that could not fire under compiled execution). FP32 master parameters, optimizer state, embedding lookup, tying, initialization, all other layers, kernels, schedule, batch, seed, evaluator, launch shape and environment are unchanged; num_params_M must remain 592.9 and all config oneliners identical to control except the one new field. No torch.autocast context, no other precision/kernel/optimizer/architecture switch. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967). Outcome classes evaluated in order: (1) HALT-INERT if STEP 0 finds both head operands already BF16 (or the call under autocast) under default flags; (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (3) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-1% of control (head matmul precision is not a measurable cost); (4) EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW if steps > +10% (>2278 trn21, >2283 trn22): compare logged validation trajectories at matched step counts before any quality claim; if matched-step trajectories are unavailable, quality attribution is recorded unresolved; SUCCESS only if public_val_bpb < control by >= 0.001 and no matched-step deficit > 0.010 at the control's final step; (5) SUCCESS if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.001; (6) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb >= control; (7) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (including +2% steps with a BPB gain smaller than 0.001).
